parallel.requirements: Recognized the Rust 2021, std-only, byte-exact CLI/output, Cargo layout, root test4.rs, and black-box reference-binary requirements.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent probed the binary and assigned essentially the full earcut implementation plus verification to one coder child rather than keeping active implementation ownership.
parallel.implementation: The child wrote Cargo.toml, test4.rs, and src/earcut.rs, built successfully, then iteratively debugged hole elimination and ear clipping behavior against the binary.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: All deliverable writes came from the child into /output; the artifact was copied and structurally valid, but there was no completed child handoff or parent integration pass.
parallel.verification: The child ran smoke and differential tests; later output showed n=0,1,2,3,5 matching while n=4 and larger selected cases still differed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The active child was cancelled before resolving known mismatches; official evaluation completed and failed with 16 of 34 passing.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Rust 2021, std-only, byte-exact CLI/output, Cargo layout, root test4.rs, and black-box binary requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single main actor owned probing, implementation, compilation, debugging, and verification locally, with no delegation or child-result lifecycle.
serial.implementation: The main actor wrote Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/earcut.rs, and test4.rs, fixed an initial compile error, and then adjusted algorithm variants locally.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial artifact was a normal Cargo project with test4.rs and library files; no cross-agent integration or handoff was involved.
serial.verification: Serial ran differential checks that exposed mismatches at n=2,3,4 and later n=2 through n=20, including empty Rust outputs for n>=5 after a bad edit.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out while debugging variant behavior; official evaluation completed and failed with 9 of 34 passing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized byte-exact Rust reimplementation, no crates, Cargo layout, root test4.rs, and binary-based debugging.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the same prompt and recognized the same output, CLI, dependency, and project structure obligations.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirements difference; both failures came from incomplete algorithmic matching rather than a missed prompt requirement.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent performed brief probing, then delegated the whole implementation and verification job to a single coder child.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The main actor kept all implementation, build, and verification ownership in one serial trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a child-result lifecycle around the only implementation owner; serial had no such ownership boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child brief included detailed CLI, output, project layout, algorithm, and verification instructions from the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor retained its own task context while directly writing the entry file and library implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no supported context-loss or interface-contract failure; the major contrast is delegation lifecycle, not missing child context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child implemented an arena-based earcut port, edited hole elimination and ear checks, and reached partial matching before cancellation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor implemented a similar earcut port, fixed a compile error, then tried variant changes that later caused broader mismatches and empty outputs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel reached a better partial implementation than serial, but both still had algorithmic output mismatches before closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The delegated implementation child remained active until cancellation and returned only a failed subagent result to the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There was no child result lifecycle; the local main actor itself reached cancellation while still debugging.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Only parallel lost the sole delegated implementation path through child termination before final handoff.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child wrote the output project directly into /output, but no concurrent sibling or parent writes collided with those files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor wrote the same deliverable classes directly in a single workspace with no cross-agent merge.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No shared-state collision distinguishes the attempts; both artifacts were structurally copied for evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child verification showed many selected cases still differed after some early cases matched, and no final all-pass verification occurred.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verification showed mismatches at n=2 through n=20 after later edits, plus timed-out background checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both used differential testing; parallel had a stronger partial result, while serial regressed to broader failures.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out after about 2407 agent seconds with the child still active and the parent blocked on the Agent call.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out after about 2406 agent seconds while the main actor was still debugging a variant-search testbed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted budget, but parallel budget closure cut off a delegated child handoff; serial closure interrupted local debugging.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations show both solutions failed, so there is no discordant pass/fail outcome. Parallel did materially better, 16 of 34 versus serial's 9 of 34, because the delegated child reached a partially corrected implementation that matched several early cases before cancellation. Serial kept all work local but regressed into broader mismatches and empty outputs for n>=5. The retained parallel coordination pattern explains a parallel adverse process state, not a pass/fail difference.
parallel_contributors: Single delegated implementation child was cancelled before a completed result was returned to the parent.
Child verification still showed known mismatches at n=4 and larger cases before cancellation.
serial_contributors: Main actor retained local ownership and compiled, but later variant changes left many tested cases mismatching or empty.
Serial had no child handoff failure, so its worse score is an ordinary implementation/debugging shortfall.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel's algorithm version matched more official cases than serial's, but both remained byte-inexact.
Serial's later edits caused n>=5 empty outputs in its local checks.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no official outcome discordance; retained label is a realized parallel adverse lifecycle contributor only

candidates.reason: The parent explicitly assigned implementation ownership to the coder child, which wrote the project files.
There were not multiple separately owned implementation components needing a missing integration owner.
The child owned and created the Cargo project, root test4.rs, library source, and executable artifact.
The child brief included implementation, build, and verification; the failure was interruption before completion, not an unowned pipeline.
The parent's initial binary probes supplied useful examples and did not create a mandatory blocking gate with an independent adverse consequence.
Parallel did not run multiple investigators as a separate completed first phase before implementation; it delegated implementation after brief probing.
No available workers were spent on auxiliary work while the critical path lacked capacity; one child owned the critical path.
Only one child was launched, with no broad fan-out or retry storm consuming the budget.
The child scope was broad, but the same stalled chain is more directly evidenced as active child termination before handoff.
The child brief included task source, output examples, CLI behavior, no-dependency rule, project layout, and verification expectations.
There were no separately owned parallel components with omitted interoperability contracts; the single child wrote the deliverable.
No known finding disappeared during transfer; the parent passed its reference observations into the child brief.
Although the child brief was long, the child consumed it and acted on it; no overload-driven unconsumed handoff is evidenced.
No receiver acted on a handoff describing a superseded workspace or requirement state.
Only one child report path existed and no incompatible returned reports reached the parent for adjudication.
The parent did not accept or present the task as complete after the child; it received a failed subagent result and the run closed.
No replacement child or retry episode occurred in the parallel trajectory.

candidates.reason: The parent delegated the full implementation to an active child; the child was still debugging known mismatches and was cancelled before returning a completed result.
candidates.realized_consequence: The delegated implementation and verification work was interrupted before a child handoff, leaving the parent with only a failed subagent result and a known partially matching artifact.
candidates.near_match_reason: The parent received the failed child result at the global cancellation point, leaving no separate post-failure recovery decision; the direct lifecycle fault is earlier child interruption.

The failed child result arrived at global cancellation, so there was no distinct parent recovery window beyond the retained termination chain.
The parent never received a completed child result to inspect, use, or reject.
The parent waited on one Agent call, but the adverse lifecycle is the same child cancellation before handoff, not a separate inspectable wait episode.
No live sibling or parent implementation path produced competing files or incompatible designs.
Only the child edited the implementation files; no two live agents edited the same source file.
No non-entry library or configuration source owned by another actor was replaced by a concurrent actor.
The required test4.rs and executable were owned by the child; no other live actor overwrote that deliverable.
There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replacing another actor's final tree work.
The shared /output workspace did not have multiple live writers causing unstable state or provenance ambiguity.
No generated file, cache, fixture, or temporary artifact from one actor was consumed by another as stable input.
